claims.text: The initial alloy is equimolar HfNbTaTiZr.
Equimolar HfNbTaTiZr exhibits a single-phase microstructure.
A factorial design can be used to systematically vary the percentages of Hf, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr.
A factorial design can decouple the effects of individual elemental-percentage variables.
Holding synthesis and heat-treatment conditions constant isolates the effects of elemental-percentage variations.
Changing elemental concentrations changes phase distribution in HfNbTaTiZr.
Changing elemental concentrations changes lattice distortion in HfNbTaTiZr.
Changing elemental percentages modulates solution strengthening.
Changing elemental percentages can promote the formation of secondary phases.
Composition-induced changes in solution strengthening and secondary phases affect dislocation mobility.
Composition-induced microstructural changes affect grain-boundary stability.
Changes in dislocation mobility and grain-boundary stability influence yield strength.
Changes in dislocation mobility and grain-boundary stability influence hardness.
Changes in dislocation mobility and grain-boundary stability influence ductility.
Non-equimolar HfNbTaTiZr samples will show statistically significant mechanical-property differences relative to the equimolar control.
The direction of the mechanical-property change depends on each element's contribution to lattice distortion and phase stability.
The equimolar HfNbTaTiZr alloy has known mechanical behavior suitable for use as a control.
Results obtained for HfNbTaTiZr under the specified processing conditions may not extrapolate to other HEA systems or processing regimes.
